title: China Has a Spring So Hot It Cooks Your Lunch · 腾冲热海 | China Travel Expert
description:
In Yunnan, a hot spring boils at 97°C — hot enough to cook your lunch in it.

This is Rehai in Tengchong, western Yunnan, where a young volcano heats the ground from below. Its famous "big boiling pot" is over three meters across and churns at 97°C day and night; lower a basket of eggs or peanuts and they're cooked in under half an hour. More than 80 springs steam across the valley, and 14 spring groups run hotter than 90°C — soak in the warm pools after your meal cooks. Autumn into winter is peak hot-spring season.

🧭 Expert Tip: Bring eggs and peanuts — vendors by the springs rent you a basket to boil your own, the local way to eat here.
